post.headline: Check account access before inviting tips
post.subtext: Recipients and staff can confirm sign-in settings and 2FA before a public tip line becomes part of a sensitive first-contact workflow.
post.image_alt_text: Social graphic showing the Hush Line desktop Authentication settings page for a recipient account. The screen shows account sign-in controls, password settings, and two-factor authentication options as part of a pre-launch source-safety checklist.

social.bluesky:
Before sharing a Hush Line address, check the recipient account behind it.

Confirm the username, keep the password current, and turn on 2FA before asking people to send sensitive information.

Add account access to the pre-launch check.
social.linkedin:
A source-safety checklist should include the recipient side of first contact.

Before a newsroom, law office, school, nonprofit, or security team points people to a Hush Line address, staff can check the account that will receive those messages: confirm the username, keep the password current, and turn on two-factor authentication where it belongs.

Make account access part of the pre-launch check before asking people to send sensitive information.
social.mastodon:
A source-safety checklist includes the recipient account, too.

Before staff share a Hush Line address, they can confirm the username, update the password, and enable 2FA so the intake account is ready for sensitive first contact.

Add account access to the pre-launch check.

post.rationale: Kept the required Authentication screenshot and source_safety_checklist format, but moved away from recent access-security posts about routine account upkeep. This draft frames authentication as one item in a recipient-run source-safety checklist before sensitive first contact begins, matching documented Hush Line use cases for journalists, lawyers, educators, nonprofits, security teams, and other trusted recipients.
post.copy_brief: Write for recipients and staff using Hush Line day to day, not for platform admins.
